text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Education minister Jo Ritzen's visit to China to renew
ties in education will pave way for future Dutch trade mission.
- Wholesalers in Netherlands threatened by shake-out due to lack of knowledge of IT technology and electronic trade. (p1)
- Belgium refuses Dutch credit insurer NCM access to its insurance market for political bad debt risks. (p1)
- Dutch textile sector recovers from three years of malaise. (p5)
- Economy in the Netherlands continues growth of about three percent in first quarter. (p6)
VOLKSKRANT
- Cabinet to put aside 250 million guilders until 2001 to limit damage to the environment caused by economic growth. (p1)
- Improved financial discipline brings state 700 million guilders from credit insurer NCM. (p2)
- Dutch engineers eye order for dismantling Philips Petroleum Company's North Sea oil rig. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- If inflation stays low, FNV union prepared to limit next year's pay demands to three percent. (p1)
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen plans ban on pig breeding to fight ongoing swine fever epidemic. (p11)
- Price range of temp agency Vedior's flotation put up from Dfl 22-37 to Dfl 37-40.
TROUW
- Parliamentary parties annoyed at not being informed about PM Wim Kok's call for help for Eastern Europe. (p1)
- Difficulty to reach Schiphol Airport by road will be greater obstacle to airport's growth than tighter noise limits. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Schiphol Airport in consortium to develop terminal in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam and an airport on the Philippines. (p11)
